newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Gaddafi says cooperating with French bombing probe.
newsitem.headline: Gaddafi says cooperating with French bombing probe.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi said on Friday his country was on its way to complying with a U.N. Security Council resolution asking it to cooperate with a French investigation into the 1989 bombing of a French airliner.
"The French judge went to Libya and was given the necessary information...and he returned home satisfied," Gaddafi said at a news conference at the end of a five-day visit to Tunisia.
"Hence, Libya has executed parts of the Security Council resolution...," he added.
The resolution, adopted in 1992, sought Libya's cooperation with a French probe into the mid-air bombing in which 170 passengers were killed.
"I consider that the problem is on its way to a solution if the United States and Britain do not interfere," Gaddafi said.
Anti-terrorist judge Jean-Louis Bruguiere visited Tripoli in July following Gaddafi's offer of cooperation in a letter sent in March to French President Jacques Chirac.
The French judiciary later announced that six Libyans allegedly involved in the bombing would be tried in absentia by next year.

Gaddafi made no mention of developments on another Security Council resolution asking Tripoli to hand over for trial two of its citizens suspected in the 1988 bombing of a Pan Am airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland in which 270 people died.
Washington and London want the two suspects tried in the United States or Britain. Gaddafi says the trial would only be acceptable in a third country.
In 1992 the U.N. imposed sanctions on Libya, including an arms and air embargo. The ban on flights to and from Libya forced Gaddafi to travel by land to neighbouring Tunisia.
